ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar) and GFSC AML/CFT Guidance Notes. All general partners, limited partners with 25% or greater holdings, and natural-person controllers must be screened against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, UK OFSI consolidated list, OFAC SDN list, and the Gibraltar financial sanctions register. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence. Screening is repeated at least quarterly and before any significant transaction event on SWIFT Wire or PayPal rails.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies House (Registry of Companies) — https://www.companieshouse.gi
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All legal names must be in Roman/Latin script; English is the sole statutory language. No transliteration to a local script is required because Gibraltar has no secondary official script. Numerals and standard punctuation are permitted. Non-Roman scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) are not accepted within the legal name but may appear as a registered alias/trading name if the Registry determines it is not misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Crown or Government (any token suggesting royal or ministerial sponsorship)
Financial services licensable activity descriptors (e.g., 'Fund', 'EMI', 'Payment') without GFSC approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written re-review request with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days, citing the statutory grounds under the Companies Act 2014 or Limited Partnerships Act 2018. Alternatively, a fresh reservation may be submitted with a distinct name. Final recourse is available via judicial review before the Gibraltar Supreme Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted for correspondence purposes, but a physical registered office in Gibraltar is mandatory for the ELP and for any Gibraltar-resident corporate general partner. The registered agent must maintain a physical presence. For this low-risk manufacturing and retail business, a virtual office meets registration requirements; however, full commercial substance (local management oversight, operational bank account, and records keeping) is recommended to preserve pass-through tax eligibility and reduce substance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Medium; quantified annual probability of unannounced on-site physical inspection is below 10% for a Low_Risk_Standard manufacturing/trading ELP with a compliant registered agent and proper statutory books. Likelihood would increase if the entity later conducts intragroup financing, property holding, or high-volume cross-border payments.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 2014 (Gibraltar); Limited Partnerships Act 1925 (as amended); Exempted Limited Partnership Regulations, particularly sections governing registration, exemption status, general partner liability, and corporate governance of the corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar — Registry of Limited Partnerships
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form ELP-01 — Application for Registration of an Exempted Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an Exempted Limited Partnership. Capital contributions are fixed by the partnership agreement and contribution schedule. Escrow accounts are not legally mandated but are strongly recommended when limited partner contributions are received before registration completion.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the board of directors of KYL General Partner Limited, as sole general partner of KY-ELP Action Figure Holdings L.P., hereby resolve: (1) that the Company subscribes for the general partner interest in the partnership upon the terms of the partnership agreement; (2) that the registered office of the partnership be established at 5/2 Gibraltar Business Centre, Europort, Gibraltar; (3) that KYL Management Services (Gibraltar) Ltd. be appointed as administrator and designated general partner representative; (4) that the authorized signatories for banking and regulatory filings be the directors named in the subscription schedule; and (5) that the officers be authorized to complete the Gibraltar Companies House registration, pay all fees, and open a Swift GBP/USD account with a licensed EMI.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House — Name Index via e-Registry online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application for 'KY-ELP Action Figure Holdings L.P.' through the Companies House e-Registry. Confirm that the name ends with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' and does not contain restricted or misleading terms. Attach the consent letter from the intended general partner.
required_dossiers: Consent letter from the intended general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is flagged as confusingly similar or misleading, file an amended reservation with a distinctive secondary name or seek a Registrar's direction to overcome the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Qualified Gibraltar legal counsel and notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement in English, incorporating the exempted status election, capital contribution schedule, profit and loss allocation, general partner authority, indemnification, and transfer restrictions. Execute the agreement before a notary public and obtain certified copies.
required_dossiers: Board resolution of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar questions the partnership agreement's compliance with Gibraltar law, amend the agreement to include the required reserved powers, general partner residency details, or exemption-specific clauses and re-submit for notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar — Registry of Limited Partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form ELP-01 together with the prescribed statement of initial capital, details of general and limited partners, registered office address, and the statutory fee. Payment is made online by card or bank transfer. Verify that all signatories execute the form in accordance with the Limited Partnerships Act.
required_dossiers: Prescribed statement on initial capital and exemptions
Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement
Certified copies of identity and address proof for each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing to the Registrar within 14 days, provide supplementary declarations, pay any supplemental fee, and re-notarize any documents that have been translated or executed by non-resident partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of certificate of registration and gazettement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Registration confirming the exempted limited partnership status. The certificate and entity particulars are filed with the official gazette where required. Retain the certificate for bank onboarding and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership
Gazette notice of formation (if requested by the Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains clerical or typographical errors, file a written request for certificate reissuance under the correction provisions of the Companies Act 2014 and provide supporting evidence of the correct particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance setup and post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House and Gibraltar Income Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting of the corporate general partner and adopt the pro-forma first board resolution. Submit the beneficial ownership register declaration, appoint the designated representative, and file the exempted status notification and tax registration particulars with the Gibraltar Income Tax Office.
required_dossiers: Appointment of designated representative and administrator
Certificate of Registration and partnership agreement extracts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Income Tax Office rejects the tax notification, correct any mismatch between the registered office, general partner details, and business activity description, and re-submit the notification with a cover letter explaining the manufacturing and retail distribution scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (DEHCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Light Environmental Impact Assessment Registration
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No direct seawater discharge. Wastewater pH must be 6-9, biochemical oxygen demand below 20 mg/L, suspended solids below 30 mg/L. VOC emissions limited to 0.5 kg/hour or 1.5 metric tons per year. All waste handling must comply with the Hazardous Waste Regulations and Gibraltar Environmental Quality Standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire and Rescue Service; structural load approval from Gibraltar Building Control; occupational workplace clearance certificate issued under the Health and Safety at Work Act covering machine guarding, noise exposure, ventilation, and emergency evacuation procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Government of Gibraltar – Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax), governed by the Income Tax Act 2010; official portal at https://www.taxation.gi; corporate registry interface via Gibraltar Companies House under the Companies Act 2014.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Exempted Limited Partnership with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2014 to obtain the ELP registration number and certificate of exemption. Step 2: Submit Form IT-ELP non-resident partnership declaration to the Income Tax Office; non-resident partners are not chargeable on foreign-source income absent a Gibraltar permanent establishment. Step 3: Obtain a Gibraltar tax reference number for the ELP and for any Gibraltar-resident partner. Step 4: For Qualifying Category 1 or Category 2 status, file the relevant application and obtain advance tax clearance from the Commissioner of Income Tax. Step 5: Appoint a Gibraltar-resident general partner and registered office; no minimum capital requirement applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – the Exempted Limited Partnership is fully tax transparent; income, gains, and losses flow through pro rata to partners, and non-resident partners are outside the charge to Gibraltar income tax unless trading through a Gibraltar permanent establishment. No entity-level corporation tax is imposed on the ELP itself.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Qualifying Category elections (Category 1 and Category 2) under the Income Tax Act 2010 are available for eligible trading activities and provide certainty of tax treatment for partners; Category 3 election applies to high-net-worth individuals. There is no US-style check-the-box regime; hybrid mismatch rules are implemented through the Taxation (Hybrid and Mismatch Arrangements) Act 2018, aligned with OECD BEPS Action 2 and the UK/Gibraltar Tax Information Exchange Agreement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT/GST/Sales and Use Tax – Gibraltar is outside the European Union VAT territory despite its UK Overseas Territory status; no general consumption tax, sales tax, use tax, or GST is levied on goods or services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not Applicable – no VAT or GST registration regime exists in Gibraltar; there is no turnover threshold, no fiscal representative requirement, and no intra-community acquisition or distance-selling registration obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not Applicable – no real-time fiscal clearance, B2B e-invoicing, SAF-T reporting, or digital stamping mandate exists in Gibraltar; commercial invoices must satisfy Income Tax Act record-keeping requirements with a 6-year retention period, but no tax-authority pre-clearance, API integration, or continuous transaction control regime applies. Excise duties are limited exclusively to fuel, alcohol, and tobacco products.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not Applicable – because Gibraltar imposes no VAT, a 0% export VAT rate does not exist; export sales of action-figure mecha model kits manufactured by the ELP are outside the scope of any Gibraltarian indirect tax, and no VAT refund mechanism or input-VAT credit claim arises.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Entry (Goods Movement Reference via the UK Customs Declaration Service or Gibraltar local export documentation)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or Bank Transfer Instruction evidencing export proceeds
Manufacturer's Certificate of Origin (for preferential tariff claims)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT clawback applies given the absence of VAT; however, the Commissioner of Income Tax may reopen assessments within 4 years, extended to 6 years for fraudulent or negligent conduct, under the Income Tax Act 2010. False customs export declarations attract penalties of up to 200% of evaded duties and forfeiture of goods under the Customs Ordinance 2011. Failure to retain export documentation for the 6-year statutory period may result in disallowance of foreign-source income exemptions for partners and default assessments at the 12.5% corporate rate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Gibraltar has no independent central bank. Banking supervision, AML/CFT oversight, and licensing are vested in the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC); the note-issuing authority is the Gibraltar Currency Commission, a unit of HM Government of Gibraltar's Treasury; the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is legal tender and is fixed at par with the British pound sterling (GBP), with the Bank of England serving as the de facto monetary anchor through the 1:1 GIP/GBP peg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies. Gibraltar maintains no exchange control legislation and no capital or current account restrictions, mirroring the UK's post-1979 liberalised regime. The GIP/GBP peg is fixed at par, so conversion into and out of GBP carries negligible currency risk; USD, EUR, and CNH/CNY conversion is freely available through the licensed banking sector. Profit remittance by the Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) to non-resident limited partners is unrestricted, and because the ELP is tax-transparent, distributions are not subject to Gibraltar withholding tax unless the partner is a Gibraltar resident or the profits are attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment. The only friction is bank-level source-of-funds verification under GFSC AML guidance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Neither the United Kingdom nor Gibraltar imposes statutory surrender timelines, mandatory conversion ratios, or repatriation windows for export receipts. The ELP may retain export proceeds in any freely convertible currency (GIP, GBP, USD, EUR, CNH) in designated foreign-currency accounts. Only statistical aggregate reporting obligations apply (GFSC monetary and balance-of-payments returns); there is no forced conversion or central-bank surrender requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banco Santander Totta S.A. - Gibraltar Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High feasibility with material legal constraints. Gibraltar is outside the EEA and UK financial-services passporting perimeter, so a UK or EU licensed EMI (e.g., Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer) cannot passport payments services into Gibraltar; it may only onboard the ELP as a customer under its proprietary safeguarding/custody model. Wise Business and Payoneer currently accept Gibraltar-registered corporate structures and are operationally well suited to sweep PayPal-sourced e-commerce proceeds; Revolut Business (UK EMI) onboards Gibraltar entities subject to FCA e-money safeguarding rules. Legal constraints: (i) funds held with an EMI are not Gibraltar bank deposits and are outside the Gibraltar Deposit Guarantee Scheme; (ii) EMIs may classify the ELP as higher risk due to the offshore-territory designation and non-resident partners, triggering enhanced due diligence, velocity monitoring, and payout caps; (iii) the EMI cannot provide trade finance or foreign-exchange hedging products. Recommended use is a collection-and-settlement sweep layer only, with core treasury liquidity parked in a GFSC tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid regime. GFSC-licensed banks, applying FATF-aligned Gibraltar AML/CFT Guidance Notes, generally require at least one live KYC interview of the General Partner or a senior UBO/controller before account activation. Since the post-2020 practice, the live session may be conducted by video, but tier-1 banks typically require one of two additional conditions: (a) all partner and entity documents certified by a Gibraltar-licensed fiduciary acting as a regulated 'introducer' under the Gibraltar certified-introducer regime, or (b) one physical attendance at a Gibraltar branch. A fully remote, zero-touch opening without a licensed introducer is not available in the tier-1 domestic banks. Costed recommendation: the ELP should appoint a Gibraltar-licensed corporate-services provider as introducer and conduct the required video interview of the General Partner; a physical director visit to Gibraltar may be avoided in most cases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore 'special territory' ELP with dispersed non-resident limited partners and outsourced overseas manufacturing flagged in the bank's jurisdiction-risk matrix.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar Registrar Certificate of Registration and Certificate of Limited Partnership; fully executed Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement with capital schedule and drawdown watermark; UBO and control table (all partners above 25% or control thresholds) with passport, proof-of-address, and MVN documents; narrative statement of economic purpose covering procurement, IP-holding, and digital sales governance from Gibraltar; Gibraltar-licensed registered-office agreement and compliance oversight letter from the licensed introducer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity PayPal and card-receivable flows with long-tail global hobby/anime customers and low average transaction values (ISIC 3240 e-commerce profile) triggering online-acceptance AML red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PayPal Business and e-commerce platform agreements; 12-month PayPal settlement reports and payout logs; order-to-inventory-to-fulfilment system trace; product catalogue with commercial invoices; refund and chargeback policy; 3PL warehousing contracts and courier consignment records proving physical movement of the action-figure mecha model kits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring trade-payable concentrations to PRC/Hong Kong injection-molding suppliers (steel tooling, ABS/PS resin, packaging), characterised as China counterparty risk in sanction- and country-risk screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: English-language supply contracts and proforma invoices; dual-language purchase orders; MT103 payment records referencing underlying purchase orders; supplier business licences (营业执照) and company-registry extracts; Incoterms matrix (FOB/CIF); bills of lading, air waybills, and customs-broker entries proving genuine import transactions; mould-tooling ownership records demonstrating commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office at a serviced or agent address with no local payroll or utility footprint, weakening the bank's entity-calibration and economic-substance assessment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar serviced-office or licensed management-company agreement; general-partner governance records (resolutions and management minutes held in Gibraltar); professional indemnity and product-liability insurance policies; letter from a licensed Gibraltar tax/fiduciary adviser confirming management and control exercised from Gibraltar; annual-return filings and bank statements reflecting local overhead payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IP-heavy anime-character and mecha-property licensing and merchandise royalty flows creating ambiguity over brand ownership, licensing authority, and the direction of royalty payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trademark registrations (UKIPO, EUIPO, USPTO, and JP as applicable); licensed-character sub-license agreements from rights-holders; IP-holding deed assigning or describing marks and royalty pass-through; royalty statements and OCML mechanics; solicitor's freedom-to-operate opinion for the snap-fit mecha model kits; licence-fee payment evidence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for LP capital injections: contributing partners wire via SWIFT MT103 with remittance information 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital - LP Contribution - [ELP Name] - [Partner Name] - Drawdown Date', referencing the IMF BPM6/CDIS direct-investment equity purpose code 110; the receiving GFSC bank is pre-notified with the executed LPA drawdown notice, the partner's source-of-funds and source-of-wealth dossier (bank statements, employment or exit-wealth evidence), and identity documents. Capital must be credited to a segregated Capital Escrow Account or a clearly demarcated capital ledger, and must not be commingled with operating revenue. PayPal-rail collections must be swept separately to the Operational Account to preserve an auditable capital-vs-revenue liquidity split. If a third-party agent wires on behalf of a partner, a written mandate and proof of the underlying partner relationship are required under GFSC AML rules.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail hierarchy for trade settlements: (i) SWIFT MT103 is the primary rail for tooling deposits, resin purchases, and finished-goods payments to PRC/Hong Kong suppliers, carrying full beneficiary CNAPS/IBAN-BIC particulars and invoice references; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600-compliant MT700 issuance, MT707 amendments, and MT756 reimbursements) is recommended for large containerised batch settlements, with the issuing Gibraltar bank examining bills of lading, inspection certificates, and packing lists against LC terms; (iii) domestic GBP clearing or Faster Payments via UK correspondent accounts is used for UK suppliers and overheads; (iv) domestic Gibraltar clearing (GIP) is used for local Gibraltar payments; (v) PayPal payouts are restricted to refunds and chargeback operations and are not used as a trade-creditor rail. Foreign-exchange conversion for outbound settlements is executed same-day to eliminate settlement-date gap exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (GBP versus USD and GBP versus CNH) under ISDA/CSA or bank master-confirmation agreements with GFSC-licensed counterparties
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY or other restrictively convertible emerging-market currencies, booked offshore to avoid PRC onshore FX controls
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (GBP/USD and GBP/CNH) covering trade-related borrowing and multi-currency liquidity needs
Vanilla FX options (GBP/USD and GBP/CNH) to cap conversion costs on uncertain PayPal settlement flows and tender-driven lumpy receipts
FX swap and rollover contracts within the same clearing bank to manage intraday treasury concentration and PayPal settlement lags

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies House - Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the date of registration of the ELP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty increases from GBP 50 to GBP 750; continued default for 6 months is an offence and may lead to administrative strike-off of the ELP registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Register of Beneficial Owners (RBO) via Companies House
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 December of each year, confirming any changes in beneficial ownership; interim updates required within 14 days of any ownership change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or updating inaccuracies attracts penalties up to GBP 1,000 per default; continuous non-compliance may result in civil sanctions and restriction on receiving certificates of good standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Office of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Tax & Customs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing for the preceding calendar year due on or before 30 September each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing penalized at GBP 500 and then GBP 1,000 for continued default; may trigger automatic presumption of inadequate substance and cross-border information exchange.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Office of the Commissioner of Income Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 90 days following the end of the partnership accounting period; statutory year-end commonly aligned to 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing assessed a maximum penalty of GBP 1,500 plus interest at 8% per annum; persistent non-compliance may lead to enforcement action against the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is required if the ELP exceeds two of the following: annual turnover above GBP 6.5 million, gross assets above GBP 3.26 million, or average staff above 50 employees; otherwise the partners may resolve to grant audit exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; a Gibraltar GAAP-equivalent (FRS 102) may be applied by private ELPs with unanimous partner consent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain an accurate register of beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation by 31 December in each calendar year; any transfer of a 25% or greater partnership interest requires a further updated RBO filing within 14 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 10% (standard Gibraltar corporation tax rate; an ELP is transparent, so corporate partners are taxed at 10% on their share of Gibraltar-source chargeable profits)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective tax for a non-resident ELP deriving no Gibraltar-source income; no VAT, capital gains tax, or wealth tax; 10% flat corporate rate for resident taxable companies; full exemption from withholding tax on outbound distributions.
